settings.chHttpsNote: Both http and https work: Feishu sends through your app credentials (the app needs im:message:send_as_bot); Slack takes an incoming webhook URL; Bluebird takes a generic-source URL; a generic webhook receives structured JSON (cert expiry, probes and metric rules share one stream).

settings.chBluebirdTokenPlaceholder: access token of the Bluebird generic source
settings.chBluebirdTokenNote: Deliveries carry Authorization: Bearer <token> — a Bluebird generic source rejects requests without one (401).
settings.chBluebirdNote: Hands alerts to the Bluebird gateway, which fans them out to Bark / Feishu / WeCom and friends. Use the webhook URL shown under Settings → Sources → generic source. Messages carry title / body plus a level (critical / warning / resolved) that Bluebird maps to its own colours.
settings.chWebhookNote: Your endpoint receives structured JSON (title / body / level / color / fields …, plus a text field for older receivers). With a token set, deliveries carry Authorization: Bearer <token>; leave it empty for no auth header.
settings.chTokenPlaceholder: leave empty for no auth header
settings.chTokenNote: Deliveries carry Authorization: Bearer <token> — useful for your own receiver.
settings.chReceiveIdPlaceholder: group chat_id (starts with oc_) / user open_id (starts with ou_)

settings.aiBrief:
# ZhiWei console API

Base: {{base}}
Auth: every request carries `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}`

## Read (GET)

- /v1/todo — the few things that need doing, bucketed as now / watch / recovered, each with a hint_key (what to do next)
- /v1/nodes — node list with the latest metric frame and online state
- /v1/nodes/<id>/series?metric=host.cpu.usage&from=<ms>&to=<ms>&limit=600 — trends; resolution=raw means 10-second data, hourly means hourly aggregates
- /v1/nodes/<id>/containers, /v1/containers — containers (compose project tags act as the "app" label)
- /v1/certificates — certificates and expiry
- /v1/services — services and probe state
- /v1/retention — retention policy (raw days, hourly days)

## Act (POST /v1/exec)

Body: {"node_id":"<id>","action":"<name>","params":{...}}
Actions: container_start / container_stop / container_restart / container_remove,
kill_process (params: pid, signal=term|kill), fetch_logs, restart_host, shutdown_host,
refresh_inventory, scan_certs
Result: GET /v1/commands/<command_id> (or /v1/commands/history for the latest 100) — state=done|failed, result_ok, result_text / result_error

## Boundaries

- Every action runs as a signed command: the ops key signs it, the node verifies before executing, and the node signs the result back.
- Do not run destructive actions (shutdown, reboot, container removal, killing processes) on your own — say what you intend to do and wait for confirmation.
- A container can only be removed once stopped; stop it first.
- Reboot and shutdown are delayed by one minute, leaving a window to cancel.
settings.pwSubtitle: Changing this key is the console's password change
settings.pwNote: This is the only key the console has (nodes use signatures and don't recognise it). It takes effect immediately, and this browser switches over too — no re-login.
settings.caEdgeNote: TLS is terminated by an edge in this deployment, so this CA isn't used: the monitor's certificate is edge-issued and nodes no longer pin it (they use system roots). The fingerprint here is only a diagnostic.
settings.enrollTokensSubtitle: One-shot bootstrap commands for new machines; they stop working once expired
settings.enrollTokensEmptyHint: Click "New" to generate a command, then run it once on the target machine's shell.
settings.enrollTokensNote: Permanent tokens come from the server's ZHIWEI_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN env var; changing it and restarting the server is how you revoke them.
settings.enrollTokenRevokeMessage: If unused, no future target machine can enroll with it after this.
settings.aiTokensSubtitle: Long-lived tokens for external agents to read cluster data; revoking disconnects all clients immediately
settings.aiTokensEmptyHint: Click "New" to generate a token, then put it in the agent's Authorization Bearer header.
settings.aiTokensNote: Plaintext is shown only once at creation time. If lost, create a new one.
settings.aiTokenRevokeMessage: After this every AI client using this token disconnects immediately. This cannot be undone.
settings.mcpSubtitle: Connect AI clients via Model Context Protocol
settings.mcpTokensSubtitle: Long-lived tokens for MCP clients; revoking disconnects all clients immediately
settings.mcpTokensEmptyHint: Click "New" to generate a token, then put it in the MCP config.
settings.mcpTokenRevokeMessage: After this every MCP client using this token disconnects immediately. This cannot be undone.
